title: Contributing content
text: This site is built using Quarto. Quarto takes a collection of Markdown files and Jupyter notebooks and renders them as a static HTML site. The Jupyter notebooks can include code cells that are executed at build time to generate tables, visualisations and other outputs.

title: Guide for authors
text:
Include extra metadata in the front matter section of a notebook. Possible values include:

authors
abstract
keywords

For example, to list the notebook’s authors add their details to the first cell of the notebook like this.
---
authors:
    - name: Tim Sherratt
      orcid: http://orcid.org/0000-0001-7956-4498
      url: https://timsherratt.au
---
Front matter rules: - has to be in the first cell of the notebook - cell has to be set to ‘Markdown’ - data has to be valid YAML - YAML data has to be enclosed top and bottom by --- lines

title: Guide for authors
text:
Labelling cells and content
By labelling code and Markdown cells they can used in cross-references or embedded elsewhere in the book.
Note that labels are accessible across the whole site, not just a notebook, so should be unique. Quarto defines a set of prefixes that should be used in labels, eg: ‘fig’, ‘tbl’, and ‘sec’ for figures, tables and sections.
To label a section, add {#sec-my-section-name} after a heading. For example:
## Cool things about Hansard {#sec-my-cool-hansard-things}
To label an image add {#fig-my-image} after the standard Markdown image embed link:
![](parliament-house.jpeg) {#fig-parliament-house}
To label an image with a caption:
::: {#fig-parliament-house}

![](parliament-house.jpeg)

Parliament House in Canberra
:::
To label a code cell that produces a chart add #| label: fig-my-chart and #| fig-caption: My interesting chart to the very top of the cell:
#| label: fig-sitting-days
#| fig-cap: Number of sitting days per year for the House of Representatives and the Senate

# Code goes here

title: Guide for authors
text:
Links and cross-references
To create an internal link to another notebook, use standard Markdown syntax with the full or relative path to the notebook in the file structure, including the file extension.
For example, [introduction to Hansard](/hansard/hansard-intro) produces:

Here’s an introduction to Hansard

To create an internal link to a heading in another notebook, use standard Markdown syntax with the full path to the notebook and the heading’s HTML id. For example to link to the ‘Quarto’ heading in the ‘contributing’ notebook, use [](/contributing/contributing#quarto):

This site uses quarto.

You can also use the @fig-sitting-days shorthand:
Figure 1 shows the number of sitting days for each house of parliament.

title: About this site
text: This site was created by the Reusable and Accessible Public Interest Documents (RAPID-CDL) project, part of ARDC’s Community Data Lab. The RAPID-CDL project aims to make public interest documents such as parliamentary proceedings, inquiry submissions, hearing transcripts, and ministerial records more accessible and usable for researchers across Australia.

title: An example notebook
text:
The cell below generates a chart. Note that the cell has been labelled using #| label: sitting-days-chart this means the cell can be referenced elsewhere using sitting-days-chart.
If you look in the cell metadata you’ll see it includes the remove-cell tag. This means the cell and its output won’t be included in the final book. Instead we’ll embed the chart in a figure below so we can add a caption and it will be automatically numbered.

import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

df = pd.read_json("https://handbookapi.aph.gov.au/api/StatisticalInformation/SittingDaysPerYear")

dfs = []
for house in ["Reps", "Senate"]:
    df_h = df[["Year", f"{house}Days"]]
    df_h["house"] = house
    df_h.columns = ["year", "days", "house"]
    dfs.append(df_h)
df_split = pd.concat(dfs)

ticks = [t for t in range(1900, 2030, 5)]
alt.Chart(df_split).mark_bar().encode(
    x=alt.X("year:O").axis(values=ticks).title(None),
    y=alt.Y("days:Q").title(None),
    row=alt.Row("house").title("number of days"),
    color=alt.Color("house").legend(None),
    tooltip=["year:O", "house:N", "days:Q"]
).properties(height=200, width=600, padding=20)









Figure 1: Number of sitting days per year for the House of Representatives and the Senate
